pictures.scene: Mihály Munkácsy, Christ before Pilate — the governor on his judgment seat while the accuser points across the floor at the silent prisoner, to the tune of Do Not Destroy a Miktam of David, do you indeed speak justly O rulers
pictures.name: pd_munkacsy_christ_before_pilate

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Conspiracy of Claudius Civilis — the conspirators crossing their swords over the table to swear their oath, do you judge uprightly O sons of men, in your hearts you devise injustice
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_conspiracy_of_claudius_civilis

pictures.scene: Francisco de Goya, The Third of May 1808 — the firing squad with their muskets levelled at the man kneeling in the lantern light, with your hands you mete out violence on the earth, the wicked are estranged from the womb
pictures.name: pd_goya_the_third_of_may_1808

pictures.scene: David Teniers the Younger, The Blind Leading the Blind — the line of blind men holding on to each other and walking straight into the ditch, the liars go astray from birth, their venom is like the venom of a snake
pictures.name: pd_teniers_the_blind_leading_the_blind

pictures.scene: Otto Marseus van Schrieck, Serpents and Insects — the snake rearing out of the undergrowth with its mouth open and its fangs showing, like a cobra that shuts its ears, refusing to hear the tune of the charmer
pictures.name: pd_van_schrieck_serpents_and_insects

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Fortune Teller — the girl holding the young man's hand and reading his palm while she slips the ring off his finger, who skillfully weaves his spell, O God shatter their teeth in their mouths
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_fortune_teller

pictures.scene: Peter Paul Rubens, Daniel in the Lions' Den — the lions crowded round the pit with their jaws open and their teeth bared, O LORD tear out the fangs of the lions, may they vanish
pictures.name: pd_rubens_daniel_in_the_lions_den

pictures.scene: Jacob van Ruisdael, A Waterfall — the river pouring white over the rocks and running away downstream, like water that runs off, when they draw the bow
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_a_waterfall

pictures.scene: Lucas Cranach the Younger, The Stag Hunt of the Elector — the hunters standing along the water with their crossbows drawn and aimed, may their arrows be blunted, like a slug that dissolves in its slime
pictures.name: pd_cranach_the_stag_hunt_of_the_elector

pictures.scene: Arnold Böcklin, The Isle of the Dead — the boat carrying its white burden toward the dark cypresses of the island, like a woman's stillborn child, may they never see the sun
pictures.name: pd_bocklin_the_isle_of_the_dead

pictures.scene: Diego Velázquez, An Old Woman Cooking Eggs — the earthen pot set over the coals before it has had time to heat through, before your pots can feel the burning thorns, whether green or dry
pictures.name: pd_velazquez_an_old_woman_cooking_eggs

pictures.scene: Gustave Courbet, The Wheat Sifters — the sieve tipped up and shaken so the chaff goes out of it onto the floor, He will sweep them away, the righteous will rejoice
pictures.name: pd_courbet_the_wheat_sifters

pictures.scene: Cristofano Allori, Judith with the Head of Holofernes — the young woman holding up the head of the tyrant for everyone to see, when they see they are avenged, they will wash their feet
pictures.name: pd_allori_judith_with_the_head_of_holofernes

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Sermon of Saint John the Baptist — the whole countryside crowded in under the trees to hear the preacher with his arm out, in the blood of the wicked, then men will say
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_sermon_of_saint_john_the_baptist

pictures.scene: Hans Memling, Christ Giving His Blessing — Christ looking straight out at the viewer with His hand raised to bless, there is surely a reward for the righteous, there is surely a God who judges the earth
pictures.name: pd_memling_christ_giving_his_blessing

lines.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David.
Do you indeed speak justly, O rulers?
Do you judge uprightly, O sons of men?
No, in your hearts you devise injustice;
with your hands you mete out violence on the earth.
The wicked are estranged from the womb;
the liars go astray from birth.
Their venom is like the venom of a snake,
like a cobra that shuts its ears,
refusing to hear the tune of the charmer
who skillfully weaves his spell.
O God, shatter their teeth in their mouths;
O LORD, tear out the fangs of the lions.
May they vanish
like water that runs off;
when they draw the bow,
may their arrows be blunted.
Like a slug that dissolves in its slime,
like a woman’s stillborn child,
may they never see the sun.
Before your pots can feel the burning thorns—
whether green or dry—
He will sweep them away.
The righteous will rejoice
when they see they are avenged;
they will wash their feet
in the blood of the wicked.
Then men will say,
“There is surely a reward for the righteous!
There is surely a God who judges the earth!”
